span_text: During the Term of this Agreement, and subject to the terms and conditions hereof, Miltenyi will non-exclusively supply and sell to Bellicum or its Licensees or Subcontractors, and Bellicum or its Licensees or Subcontractors will purchase from Miltenyi, Miltenyi Products listed on Exhibit B solely for the Permitted Use (as defined below).
segment_text: 2.1 Supply of Product. During the Term of this Agreement, and subject to the terms and conditions hereof, Miltenyi will non-exclusively supply and sell to Bellicum or its Licensees or Subcontractors, and Bellicum or its Licensees or Subcontractors will purchase from Miltenyi, Miltenyi Products listed on Exhibit B solely for the Permitted Use (as defined below). Each Purchase Order placed 5 Miltenyi Biotec-Bellicum Supply Agreement (Execution Copy, March 27, 2019) under this Agreement shall be exclusively governed by the terms and conditions of this Agreement and the Quality Agreement, as amended from time to time, unless specifically otherwise agreed between the Parties in writing. Any terms and conditions of any Purchase Order or acknowledgement given or received which are additional to or inconsistent with this Agreement or the Quality Agreement shall have no effect and such terms and conditions are hereby excluded and rejected.
annotator_notes:
Batch 6, hard-queue position 3 of seed 6102026. C04-017 S2 [23:363], the FIRST of TWO items from this sentence; C04-15 is the purchase half. Reviewer-approved field by field, with the temporal ruled separately after a grammar-level check (below).

SPLIT (sections 4.3 / 4.2). S2 states a supply duty on Miltenyi and a purchase duty on Bellicum. TWO DIFFERENT OBLIGORS and two different performances, and one item has one obligor slot, so it cannot be one item however section 4.3 is read -- ordinary independent breachability, NOT section 4.3.2's self-performance-vs-third-party shape and NOT section 8.4's mutual_obligation (that class is ONE duty imposed identically on both parties, C17-021's 'shall each use', which this is not: supply and purchase are different performances).

SPANS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL BETWEEN THE TWO ITEMS, and that is C04-04/C04-05's situation rather than a defect. The shared object phrase 'Miltenyi Products listed on Exhibit B solely for the Permitted Use' sits at [277:343], AFTER both verb phrases, so neither item's minimal span (section 3.1) is shorter than the other's: both run [23:363]. C04-04/C04-05 are locked with identical spans [4,207] and known_gaps [], so identical spans earn no tag. Section 4.2's v0.36 content-based tie-break on action_accept_set membership applies and is CONCLUSIVE here, because the two sets are disjoint -- {PROVIDE, TRANSFER, DELIVER} against C04-15's {PROCURE} -- so it never falls through to the ascending-item_id fallback.

COMPOUND ACTION -- section 8.3's branch determinant RUN, not assumed. Section 4.3 first: 'supply and sell' are two aspects of ONE indivisible performance over one shared object (Miltenyi hands the Products over and title passes against payment; neither is performable alone under this clause), so ONE item -- section 8.3 branch-1 shape, like 'provide ... and keep current'. Then the v0.47 determinant: a dropped verb triggers branch 3 only if it is neither a taxonomy member nor defensibly mappable to the verb in `action`. Section 8.8.2's 'same performance?' test: `supply` -> PROVIDE (supplying goods IS providing them; looser fits are already accepted, section 8.8's arrange->PROCURE), and `sell` -> TRANSFER rather than PROVIDE, because a sale moves TITLE and PROVIDE does not denote that. DIFFERENT taxonomy verbs, so branch 1: one item, primary verb in `action`, full verb phrase verbatim here, tag `compound_action` -- NOT branch 2 (which would require both verbs to map to the same verb, the indemnify/hold-harmless doublet shape). The full phrase is 'will non-exclusively supply and sell to'. `SELL` itself is OFF-taxonomy, execution-checked and already on record: C11-03's v0.55 ruling struck SELL from an accept-set on exactly that ground. Primary verb is `supply` -- first verb, section heading '2.1 Supply of Product', and a Supply Agreement.

TEMPORAL -- 'During the Term of this Agreement' [23:56] is UNREPRESENTABLE ON SLOT ARITY, and this verdict was reached at the GRAMMAR layer rather than off the classifier, because the classifier alone cannot distinguish the two cases section 8.6.1 separates. Verified by execution against the real parser, with a known-answer gate run first (a two-ISO DURING must parse, a bare DURING must be rejected -- and the gate caught TWO malformed harnesses before it passed):
  - `DURING "the Effective Date".."the expiry of the Term"` PARSES, giving UnresolvedDate on both bounds. So the slots are NOT ISO-only: grammar/obligation.lark reads `datetime_ref: DATE | ALIAS` with `ALIAS: ESCAPED_STRING`, and its own comment says an alias 'compiles to an UNRESOLVED DateRef'. THE IR CAN HOLD AN ALIAS-BOUNDED INTERVAL.
  - `DURING "the Term of this Agreement"` -- a SINGLE-slot form -- is REJECTED. `interval: datetime_ref '..' datetime_ref` makes BOTH bounds mandatory; there is no one-slot named-period production.
  - `DURING "the Term of this Agreement".."the Term of this Agreement"` parses, and is REFUSED as an annotation: it asserts the period's start EQUALS its end, which is false of the Term and is section 9.1 ground 2's knowing unfaithfulness.
So the form demands TWO bound references and the text supplies ONE period name; the Effective Date and the expiry are defined elsewhere in the document, outside this span, and section 3.5's span-scoped strictness forbids importing them. NO FAITHFUL DSL STRING EXISTS, which is what rules out 'representable-but-unreachable' -- that verdict requires a faithful string the classifier merely cannot produce (section 8.6.1's within_preposition case, where amount, unit and trigger are all in the span and only the preposition blocks the regex). Here nothing the classifier could do would help. `temporal: null` is therefore the null section 8.6.1 licenses. Reachability is ALSO absent and is the weaker fact: `_DURING_RE` is `^during <ISO>..<ISO>$`, so 'During the Term of this Agreement' classifies to None -- but that is a second, independent failure and NOT the ground.

NOT TAGGED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT CALLED F25 INSTANCE TWO -- the mechanism does not match. F25 is scoped to the EVENT-BOUNDED interval class and states its mechanism as 'an interval bounded by the pendency of an event has no slot in it at any surface form'; its measured population is force-majeure and state-suspension language ('for so long as' x6, 'for the duration of' x5, 'during the pendency of' x2). 'the Term of this Agreement' is a DEFINED-TERM PERIOD, which section 8's gap table has carried as its OWN separate row ('during the Term -- _DURING_RE needs two ISO dates') since before F25 existed. AGAINST MY OWN FRAMING, AND FLAGGED FOR WHOEVER RULES F25: the execution above also weakens F25's STATED mechanism, since an alias IS a legal DateRef, so 'the pendency of such challenge' would fill an UnresolvedDate slot just as happily -- meaning F25's real obstacle is arity too, not slot type. That is NOT acted on here: F25's classification and population are a dated record and not this item's to re-rule. F25 is unminted either way, so no tag is available; `known_gaps` carries `compound_action` alone, and the fallback coincides with C10-03's treatment (temporal null, vague_temporal_phrase null, no temporal tag).
COST OF THE UNTAGGED TEMPORAL IS ZERO FOR THIS ITEM, which is the difference from C10-03: `compound_action` is REPRESENTATIONAL, so section 9.1 excludes C04-14 from the in-force denominator regardless. C10-03 is untagged outright and therefore sits IN that denominator carrying F25's priced cost; this item does not.

CONDITIONS -- section 3.8's removal test applied to both candidate phrases, and C04-12's span read from its JSON before being cited.
  - 'solely for the Permitted Use' [315:343] IS an entry. Direct citation: C04-12 (same document, locked at v0.65) carries 'solely for the purpose of the Permitted Use' in its own `conditions` array with object_class plain `product`. The removal test agrees: delete it and Miltenyi owes supply for purposes beyond the Permitted Use, so the circumstances in which the duty applies change, while the set of THINGS ('Miltenyi Products listed on Exhibit B') is untouched -- condition, not object scope.
  - 'subject to the terms and conditions hereof' [62:104] is NOT an entry, and the removal test has no cell for why. Delete it and NOTHING changes: the duty is subject to the agreement's terms regardless, because it IS a term of the agreement. It is vacuous self-reference -- neither a condition (duty's circumstances unchanged) nor object scope (object's extent unchanged), where section 3.8's test is a binary. Nearest sibling is v0.54's reviewable-standard rule, which also excludes on a third ground. QUEUE ROW OPENED: section 10.1 F36, OPENED 2026-10-07 BY C04-017, case-law only.

'NON-EXCLUSIVELY' IS MANNER, NOT A CONDITION. 'will non-exclusively supply and sell' -- the adverb says the dealing is non-exclusive, i.e. HOW the duty is performed, not WHETHER it applies. The removal test returns nothing: delete it and the duty applies in the identical circumstances to the identical things, and only the exclusivity character of the arrangement changes. Same shape as v0.54's reviewable-standard ruling (a phrase governing how a right is exercised is not a conditions entry). It is kept inside the span because it sits mid-verb-phrase and section 3.1's minimal span cannot exclude it.

'LISTED ON EXHIBIT B' IS OBJECT SCOPE AND DOES NOT DISQUALIFY THE SEGMENT. Exhibit B is OUT of segment, so F24's discriminator is the one that governs (F30: F24 reaches out-of-segment references only; an in-segment referent never reaches it). F24 asks whether the reference supplies something a scored value's TRUTH depends on, or merely which instances / procedural mechanics. Here it is the latter: `object_class` is `product`, determinable from the span's own 'Miltenyi Products' head noun with Exhibit B unresolved, and the exhibit only narrows WHICH products are covered -- section 3.8's object-scope side of the removal test verbatim ('the duty is unchanged and only the set of things it covers is broader'). So section 2's cross-reference row (scored-field dependence, v0.28, not mere presence) does not exclude, and the phrase is in NEITHER `conditions` NOR a narrowed `object_class`.

PARTIES. obligor `Miltenyi` -- section 3.5.1 step 1 'Yes' branch, individually named, obligor_accept_set [] (no co-obligor or alternative). obligee `Bellicum` -- FIRST-NAMED of 'Bellicum or its Licensees or Subcontractors' [155:198].
THIS IS THE FIRST DISJUNCTIVE OBLIGEE IN THE GOLD SET -- measured, not assumed: zero of the 60 locked items carry ' or ' in `obligee`. The alternatives are recorded HERE rather than in an accept-set, because section 3.5.1 says in terms that 'for the obligee slot there is no accept-set field -- measured at joint 0 / disjunctive 3 of 1,547 pool segments and 0 of the 18 locked items (section 20.4, F4) -- so record the alternatives verbatim in annotator_notes instead'. Confirmed against data: `obligee_accept_set` appears on 0 of 60 items while `obligor_accept_set` appears on all 60. THE ALTERNATIVES, VERBATIM: 'Bellicum', 'its Licensees', 'its Subcontractors', and the whole coordinated phrase 'Bellicum or its Licensees or Subcontractors'. The coordination is DISJUNCTIVE ('or'); section 3.5.1 annotates conjunctive and disjunctive identically and asks that which it is be recorded. NOTE FOR WHOEVER REVISITS F4: section 3.5.1's v0.33 rider requiring the whole coordinated phrase in the accept-set is scoped to `obligor_accept_set` (C02-01's case, an obligor), so it has no obligee counterpart to apply; the model emitting the whole disjunction at an obligee slot would therefore fail clause 4 with no accept-set to rescue it -- the same exposure the rider was created to close on the obligor side, now live on the obligee side for the first time.
